trial_court: Court of Sh. Vidya Prakash, Special Judge (PC Act) (ACB)-01
facts_of_case: The accused was facing trial in respect of offences punishable u/s 7 & 13(1)(d) r/w 13(2) of The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

legal_principles.principle: The prosecution must prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt like any other criminal offence.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Supreme Court has ruled that the prosecution has to prove the charge thereunder beyond reasonable doubt like any other criminal offence and that the accused should be considered innocent till it is established otherwise by proper proof of demand and acceptance of illegal gratification, which are vital ingredients necessary to be proved to record a conviction.
cited_cases: A. Subair v. State of Kerala, (2009) 6 SCC 587
keywords: demand and acceptance of illegal gratification
use_in: cases under Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988

legal_principles.principle: Proof of demand and acceptance of illegal gratification by a public servant as a fact in issue is a sine qua non to establish the guilt of the accused.
legal_principles.held: In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the proof of demand and acceptance of illegal gratification by a public servant as a fact in issue is a sine qua non.
cited_cases: Neeraj Dutta v. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2023) 4 SCC 731
